At ispace U.S., we’re not just going to the Moon—we’re redefining how we get there. Our missions push the boundaries of human and robotic exploration, driven by our belief: “Expand our Planet. Expand our Future.” By providing cost-effective lunar transportation, we are pioneering a future where space is within reach for scientific discovery, commercial ventures, and sustainable exploration.  
With locations in Japan, Luxembourg, and the United States, ispace is rapidly growing and leading the way in lunar exploration and development. Our U.S. branch is based in Englewood, Colorado, and focuses on high-capacity payload lunar landers designed to support future lunar missions. Our team is made up of innovators, problem-solvers, and visionaries committed to making space more accessible and fostering the next generation of space exploration.

This application is open until  11/1/2026 or maximum applicant capacity is reached.    ispace Technologies US. located in Denver, Colorado is a looking for  highly motivated and talented college students to join our team for a summer internship like no other! You will have hands on experience with projects that are vital to our missions!     The successful candidate will be capable of taking initiative and solving problems in a fast-paced environment. Candidates should possess the ability to effectively communicate and manage relationships to deliver results.    This is a 12 week program running May to August 2027.  

What You Will Do

As an ispaceUS intern, you will become part of a collaborative team and have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful work supporting our organization and missions. Depending on your assigned department, responsibilities may include:

  • Supporting active projects, programs, and day-to-day team activities

  • Applying classroom knowledge to real-world technical or business challenges

  • Working alongside engineers, technical specialists, and business professionals

  • Participating in team meetings, project reviews, and collaborative problem-solving

  • Conducting research, analysis, documentation, testing, or project support relevant to your area

  • Learning about the commercial space industry and the development and operation of lunar missions

  • Presenting your work and accomplishments at the conclusion of the internship

What You Will Need

Have completed a minimum of two years of college-level coursework by the start of the Summer 2027 internship

Be currently enrolled in an accredited college or university and continuing their education following the internship

Be pursuing a degree relevant to the internship area for which they are being considered

Demonstrate strong communication, collaboration, organization, and problem-solving skills

Be comfortable working in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment

Demonstrate curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn

Must be able to work in-person,  full-time (paid hourly) for 12 weeks at our Englewood, CO location  beginning in May 2027 

What Makes You Stand Out

Ability to work in a fast-paced design and development environment Capable of working both independently and in a team environment Strong coordination, organization, teaming and communication abilities Familiarity with Agile software engineering practices and processes Previous engineering internship experience (aerospace preferred)

What You Can Expect

The ispaceUS Summer Internship Program is designed to provide more than just work experience. Interns will have opportunities to learn about different areas of the company, build professional relationships, develop career skills, and gain exposure to the challenges and opportunities of working in the commercial space industry.

We want our interns to leave the summer with meaningful accomplishments, new skills, professional connections, and a better understanding of where their careers could take them.

Compensation

Intern roles are non exempt (overtime eligible, as authorized) hourly positions paid at $28/hr Housing stipend paid @$300/week At ispace, we believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and experiences, even if you don’t meet every listed requirement. If you’re passionate about our mission and think you can contribute, we encourage you to apply. Your unique skills and experiences may be exactly what we need to grow and succeed together. 
To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
